title: Hypertrophy Q&A #10
summary: Tenth hypertrophy Q&A covering microloading, warm-ups, legs without weights, carries, recovery and frequency, long-armed pressing, tonnage sacrifice, baseline and evolving rep ranges, quad shape, ribcage expansion, dead hangs, paused vs touch-and-go bench, rest times, imbalances and more. NH stresses utilitarian, non-dogmatic programming, patience and controlling fatigue.
claims: Microloading is a good way to extend linear progression on presses; accept smaller jumps to keep progressing
The worst effect of a plateau is psychological
Microloading will eventually stall too; then combine it with rep and set manipulation
Matt Wenning-style high-rep warm-ups aren't ideal for bodybuilding; GPP is sport-specific and a bodybuilder's GPP is cardiovascular, best done with giant sets
Warm-ups only need to rehearse the pattern and send blood and synovial fluid; doing too much just taxes the system
His squat warm-up: 12 with the empty bar, 10 with one plate, 8 with two plates, 4 at 275 lb, then doubles at 315, 335, 365 up to 395 lb
300-rep warm-ups are junk volume that still counts as tonnage; 100 reps of bench with 145 lb won't grow your chest
You can't build maximal leg size without weights; calisthenics athletes have average legs, around 24-25 inches, and weak posterior chains
Weighted hip hinges and knee flexions are necessary for real leg development
Farmer's carries build forearms and hips but are very taxing; program them like a deadlift or squat
Yoke walks are of little use for hypertrophy: heavy loading but no flexion or weighted stretch
Sandbag carries and tosses are good low-impact GPP, and carrying the bag high with shrugging trains the yoke
For cardio and GPP NH hikes in the mountains, swims and sprints in the pool
Don't multitask between sets; he giant-sets with no rests, looping back once he reaches exercise five, and only listens to podcasts during strength rests
MMA and lifting draw from the same recovery pot; start MMA with one day a week and assess fatigue
Deadlifts Monday then barbell rows Tuesday won't work because they share muscles; pull-ups then pullovers can, depending on fatigue
Take 10-15% from each day of an overloaded 3-day program to create a shorter 4th day; all sessions become higher quality
Long-armed lifters don't need to touch the chest on the bench; reduce the ROM and try inclines, dips or push-ups
He dislikes the incline press because people wrongly assume it covers both bench and overhead press
No law says horizontal pressing must outnumber vertical; if shoulders are the goal, do more vertical pressing
Choose dumbbell overhead extensions over diamond push-ups; 3 weekly sets of long-head work suit a beginner, he schedules 9-12
For rock climbers prioritize long-head triceps; the chest is dead weight for climbing
Tonnage sacrifice: once a muscle reaches your goal, cut its volume gradually (e.g. 8 to 6 to 4 weekly sets); half volume at matched intensity maintains it
He maintains chest, triceps and biceps and sandbags quads, reallocating that tonnage to long-head triceps, upper back and hamstrings
Your baseline doesn't change with the program, only the route to reach it; evolving sets and rep ranges let you stop exactly at baseline
You're doing too much volume if soreness lingers or you can't replicate performance from one session to the next; cut volume
The old-era 'carrot quad' comes from unilateral, toes-forward work like lunges and Bulgarian split squats; heavy toes-out squats build the outer sweep
For a carrot-quad look skip a dedicated leg day: 3 upper days plus 1 hinge-focused lower day, with unilateral work spread across upper days
The ribcage can expand after puberty via pullovers stretching the costal cartilage; clavicles cannot, and his are unchanged after 15 years
Pullovers made the biggest change to his physique; part of the lat gain is structural
Always train legs for long-term integrity; to maintain without growing, squat 3x5 at 2 RIR and RDL 3x12 every 10 days
At 15-20 weekly sets per muscle with slow strength gains, try decreasing volume to train more intensely
He looked barely passable for 5-6 years and really good only 9-10 years in; beginners should build a mental and intellectual base, not rush
Barbell hack squats and behind-the-back deadlifts are hybrids; behind-the-back deadlifts are mostly a hinge with little quad work
Never alternate sets of two heavy lower-body lifts such as conventional deadlifts and hack squats
You can't decide curl technique from biceps insertions; test it yourself. He tells people not to go all the way down on curls
Weighted dead hangs don't grow lats: without scapular retraction the lat is disengaged; the lat's real max stretch is just before losing retraction
A YouTuber did weighted dead hangs for 3 months and saw no lat difference
For lat stretch use weighted pull-ups with proper form, seal rows or dumbbell rows
Touch-and-go bench is mostly ego and momentum; paused bench gives the same chest stretch; the ideal is a slow negative with a controlled micro-pause rebound
He does touch-and-go with a Slingshot only as a warm-up before paused work
He tracks weekly and daily volume per muscle by memory and adds or removes sets and reps through evolving sets
A football player maxing front squats twice a week can add a third leg day of hack squat or leg press, 4 x 10-15
He prefers Pendlay rows to seal rows for bracing and slight posterior-chain work and hates a chest pad; in a proper Pendlay the lower back stays still
On variations ignore percentages; pick a weight that fits the rep range
Evolving rep ranges: on a heavy 3-5 lift get 5,4 before adding weight; on an 8-12 isolation, 11,10 is enough to jump
On a 6-10 range start around 6,5 and add reps weekly until about 10,9,8, then jump
Rugby players' big legs come from crouched hinging and knee flexion on the field plus body fat; sled work grows legs if the hips are low
Adjustable benches are flimsier and narrower than flat ones; he never trains on an incline so he uses flat
Imbalances come from your dominant side taking more work; fix them with 3 extra unilateral sets at the end of the workout
One of his biceps is bigger and the other stronger, because a lower shoulder made it compensate
Rest times matter: rest just enough for the muscle to return to baseline; 20 s between curl sets gives a third of the reps
Losing power out of the hole: you're losing position, going deeper than hamstring flexibility allows, or losing your brace
Hold your breath on the descent and exhale only on the way up
PPL-rest-repeat can allow more intensity than PPLPPL-rest
He never changes his exercise roster; keep 6-7 favorite lifts per muscle in rotation for consistent progress; same program for 4 years
Small head and big back: grow your hair out and train neck and traps
Biceps grow from chin-ups and pulling, but find a curl variation you love; nobody hates every curl
Combine rings for the upper body with barbells for the lower body; be utilitarian, not dogmatic
With 5 kg dumbbell jumps, extend the rep range to 15 so you can drop to 5-6 reps after the jump
A real women's program is coming, not a men's program painted pink
Street lifting builds the best natty upper backs and strong mindsets, though it's limited for legs; 30-minute minimalists get mogged by park lifters
The calisthenics skill he'd most like to learn is the iron cross
He is a cat person: a cat lived 21 years, his current cat is 19, and Siamese is his favorite breed
